title: Queueable, Batch, Scheduled, and Future Apex
objectives: Choose Queueable, Batch, Scheduled, or Future Apex using the official Asynchronous Apex when-to-use table.
Explain why Salesforce recommends Queueable over future methods (job Id, non-primitives, chaining).
Cite Execution Governors and Limits for enqueue, future, batch concurrency, scheduled count, and daily async executions without inventing numbers.
Connect rollback of the parent transaction to cancelled queued jobs, and scheduled Apex to synchronous per-transaction limits.
diagnostic_question: You must call an external API with an sObject payload after a trigger save, nightly clean millions of LAB_ rows, and run a weekly maintenance job. Which async Apex types do you pick, and which official limits would you check first?
definition: Asynchronous Apex runs in the background when resources are available, in a new transaction with its own governors. The Developer Guide's choice table: Queueable for long work with a job Id, complex types, and chaining; Scheduled to run a class on a schedule; Batch for large volumes or query results bigger than a regular transaction; Future for long work, callouts, or mixed-DML isolation—though Salesforce recommends Queueable instead of future methods. ([Asynchronous Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_async_overview.htm); [Queueable Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_queueing_jobs.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: Wrong job type shows up as Flex Queue backups, daily async exhaustion, or 'we cannot find the future job.' Interviewers want Queueable vs Batch vs Future vs Scheduled with cited limits, not a vibe.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a restaurant ticket rail. Queueable is a numbered ticket you can chain and pass a whole plate (sObjects). Salesforce recommends it over future, which is a shout into the kitchen with only primitive tickets and no job Id. Batch is catering in pans: start/execute/finish, QueryLocator up to 50 million, five active jobs plus 100 in the Flex Queue. Scheduled is the printed daily prep list—100 concurrent scheduled Apex classes (5 in Developer Edition); the execute still uses synchronous per-transaction limits. Parent rollback throws the tickets away.
deeper_explanation: Asynchronous Apex is a choice among four official features, not a single annotation. Queueable: long operation, job Id, complex types, chaining. Scheduled: run on a schedule. Batch: large volume or larger query results. Future: long method, callouts, mixed DML segregation. Salesforce recommends Queueable instead of future methods. ([Asynchronous Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_async_overview.htm))

Queueable implements Queueable and System.enqueueJob. Benefits versus future: AsyncApexJob Id, member variables that are sObjects or custom types, chaining. Up to 50 enqueueJob calls per synchronous transaction; only 1 from an asynchronous transaction. Developer and Trial chained depth default 5. Rollback of the parent transaction drops queued jobs. Minimum delay 0–10 minutes exists; delay 0 plus chaining can burn the daily async limit. ([Queueable Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_queueing_jobs.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Batch implements Database.Batchable with start, execute, finish. Each execute is a discrete transaction; governors reset per execute; earlier successful executes stay committed if a later one fails. QueryLocator in start bypasses the usual SOQL row cap and can return up to 50 million records; an Iterable does not get that bypass. Platform limits: 5 batch jobs queued or active concurrently; 100 in Holding on the Flex Queue; 1 concurrent start() execution. ([Use Batch Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_batch_interface.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Scheduled Apex implements Schedulable. Maximum 100 scheduled Apex classes concurrently (5 in Developer Edition). Actual run time can delay. The scheduler runs as system. Although scheduled Apex is asynchronous, synchronous per-transaction limits apply to the scheduled job. Prefer System.scheduleBatch or a Schedulable that only kicks Batch/Queueable rather than doing heavy work in execute. Do not schedule from a bulk trigger without guaranteeing you will not exceed 100. ([Apex Scheduler](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_scheduler.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Future methods are static, void, primitives/collections of primitives only—no sObjects (stale overwrite risk). @future(callout=true) for callouts. You cannot call future from future. Per invocation: 50 future calls synchronously; 0 from batch and future contexts; 50 from queueable context. Daily async executions (batch, future, Queueable, scheduled) are 250,000 or licenses × 200, whichever is greater. Salesforce recommends Queueable instead. ([Future Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_invoking_future_methods.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant ticket rail: Queueable is a numbered ticket you can chain; Future is a shout with no ticket number; Batch is catering pans; Scheduled is the daily prep list printed the night before.
useful_mapping: whole plate on the ticket → sObject / custom-type members
shout into the kitchen → @future (primitives only, no job Id)
catering pans → Batch start / execute / finish
five ovens plus a holding rack of 100 → concurrent batch + Flex Queue Holding
thrown-away tickets when the table cancels → parent transaction rollback
new ticket window after commit → new async transaction (APEX-010)
where_it_breaks: Scheduled Apex still uses synchronous per-transaction limits—the prep list is not a bigger oven.
Batch execute order is not guaranteed even if pans were numbered.
Cursors plus chained Queueable are a documented alternative to Batch; this lesson only points at that Guide page.
The kitchen analogy does not encode named credentials or platform events.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I pick from the official table: Queueable for job Id, sObjects, and chaining; Batch for millions of rows via QueryLocator; Scheduled for the clock; Future only for mixed DML or legacy callouts. Salesforce recommends Queueable over future. Rollback of the parent save drops queued jobs.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with volume and timing. Nightly millions: Batch, knowing 5 active plus 100 Flex Queue Holding, and that each execute commits separately. After-trigger callout with an Account in memory: Queueable, 50 enqueue in the sync trigger, only 1 if I chain from async. I will not fan out 50 futures from a queueable without a reason. Scheduled execute uses synchronous limits, so I only kick Batch. Daily async is 250,000 or licenses times 200. I cite Execution Governors and Limits rather than Trailhead round numbers when they disagree.

terminology.plain: A numbered background job you enqueue.
terminology.precise: Class implementing Queueable; System.enqueueJob returns AsyncApexJob Id; supports sObjects/custom types and chaining. Recommended over future.
terminology.example: LAB_AllocQueueable holding a LAB_Order__c member, enqueued from a trigger after commit path.
terminology.non_example: A before-save Flow field update is not Queueable.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Future method: overlapping use cases, fewer features.
terminology.boundary: 50 enqueue per sync transaction, 1 from async; DE/Trial chain depth 5.

terminology.precise: Database.Batchable with start, execute, finish. QueryLocator can return up to 50 million and bypasses the usual SOQL row governor; each execute is its own transaction.
terminology.example: Nightly LAB_ArchiveBatch querying all closed LAB_ cases.
terminology.non_example: A for-loop of 200 updates in a trigger is not Batch.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queueable plus cursors: documented alternative when Flex Queue is saturated.

terminology.plain: Run this class when the clock says so.
terminology.precise: Schedulable.execute; System.schedule or Setup. Max 100 concurrent scheduled Apex (5 in DE). Runs as system. Execution may delay. Uses synchronous per-transaction limits.
terminology.example: LAB_NightlySched that only Database.executeBatch's a batch class.
terminology.non_example: Workflow time-based actions are not Scheduled Apex.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queueable delay 0–10 minutes: not a cron replacement.
terminology.boundary: Do not System.schedule from a bulk trigger without a uniqueness guard.

terminology.precise: @future static void with primitive arguments only. Optional callout=true. Used for callouts and mixed DML. Cannot call future from future. Salesforce recommends Queueable instead.
terminology.boundary: 50 per sync invocation; 0 from batch/future; 50 from queueable.

terminology.plain: The monitoring row for a background job.
terminology.precise: sObject you query with the Id enqueueJob or BatchableContext returns. Queueable processed-batches fields stay zero.
terminology.example: SELECT Status FROM AsyncApexJob WHERE Id = :jobId
terminology.non_example: CronTrigger is the scheduled-job monitor, not Queueable.
terminology.boundary: No job Id is a reason not to choose @future for new work.

terminology.plain: Holding area for extra Batch jobs.
terminology.precise: Batch jobs beyond the 5 active/queued sit Holding, max 100. Async overview warns jobs can pile up and delay critical work.
terminology.example: Sixth Database.executeBatch while five run: Holding.
terminology.non_example: The 50 enqueueJob cap is not the Flex Queue.
terminology.boundary: Cursors + Queueable are the Guide's flexibility alternative.

terminology.precise: 250,000 or applicable licenses × 200, whichever is greater, across batch (start/execute/finish each count), future, Queueable, and scheduled.
terminology.example: A Batch of 10,000 executes can throw AsyncApexExecutions Limit exceeded if remaining capacity is 9,500.
terminology.non_example: Per-transaction CPU is not this org limit.
terminology.boundary: Check REST limits resource rather than guessing remaining capacity.

terminology.plain: Starting the next Queueable from execute.
terminology.precise: One child per parent when enqueueing from an executing job. DE/Trial max stack depth 5. Delay 0 with chaining can burn daily async.
terminology.example: LAB_PageQueueable enqueues the next page of Ids.
terminology.non_example: Calling 50 Queueables from one async execute (over the 1-job async enqueue limit).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Batch finish kicking another batch: a different pattern with the 5-active cap.
terminology.boundary: Implement a halt/delay fail-safe as the Queueable page warns.

when_to_use: When a trigger must finish quickly and you need Queueable Apex for a callout with sObject state and a job Id.
When nightly maintenance must scan large volumes via Batch Apex QueryLocator (Guide: up to 50 million) rather than one transaction.
When work must run on a clock: Scheduled Apex that kicks Batch or Queueable, not a heavy execute body.
When mixed DML (setup + non-setup) still forces a Future method, with a comment that Queueable is otherwise preferred.
When chaining follow-up work needs Queueable rather than future-from-future (illegal) or 50-future fan-out.
When you must cite enqueueJob 50/1, scheduled 100, batch 5+100, and daily async 250,000-or-licenses×200 from Execution Governors and Limits.
when_not_to_use: Do not use Batch Apex for a single-record callout that Queueable Apex already fits—Flex Queue is a scarce org resource.
Do not use Future Apex for new designs that need a job Id, sObjects, or chaining; Salesforce recommends Queueable.
Do not use Scheduled Apex execute as a place to run 150 DML of heavy work; it uses synchronous per-transaction limits.
Do not System.schedule from an unsynchronized bulk trigger; you can exceed 100 scheduled classes.
Do not treat async as a way to survive parent rollback—queued Queueable/future jobs are dropped.
Do not invent daily or batch-size numbers; quote the governors and Batch pages or mark Needs verification.
configuration_or_code_location: Apex class implementing Queueable, Database.Batchable, or Schedulable; @future methods on a service class.
Setup → Apex Jobs; Setup → Scheduled Jobs; CronTrigger / AsyncApexJob SOQL.
Setup → Apex Settings for default Queueable enqueue delay (1–600 seconds) if used.
Test.startTest / Test.stopTest in the test class (APEX-016).

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox: after LAB_Order__c commits, call an allocator API with the order sObject. Nightly, archive millions of closed LAB_Case__c. Weekly, schedule that archive. No production data.

decisions.decision: Queueable for the allocator callout, holding the LAB_Order__c member.
decisions.because: Official table: job Id, complex types, callout-friendly; recommended over @future.
decisions.rejected: @future with an sObject argument (illegal) or 50 future fan-out.

decisions.decision: Batch with QueryLocator for the archive.
decisions.because: Large volume and QueryLocator bypass of the usual retrieved-row governor, up to 50 million.
decisions.rejected: Chaining Queueable with delay 0 and no halt, which the Queueable page warns can exhaust daily async.

decisions.because: Scheduled Apex uses synchronous limits; 100 concurrent scheduled cap; keep execute thin.
decisions.rejected: SOQL of all cases inside Schedulable.execute.

configuration_or_code: System.enqueueJob(new LAB_AllocQueueable(order)); on the success path after DML.
public class LAB_ArchiveBatch implements Database.Batchable<sObject> with Database.getQueryLocator('SELECT Id FROM LAB_Case__c WHERE IsClosed = true').
System.schedule('LAB weekly archive', cron, new LAB_ArchiveSched()); in a one-time anonymous script, not a trigger.

verification: Force a trigger exception: no AsyncApexJob for LAB_AllocQueueable.
Query AsyncApexJob after a successful order: Status moves from Queued/Processing.
Count CronTrigger for the LAB weekly job does not grow on each order insert.
worked_example.self_explanation: I matched the official when-to-use table: Queueable for the callout payload, Batch for volume, Scheduled as a thin clock.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; synthetic LAB_ objects; no real endpoints (use a mock in tests; APEX-013 owns mock depth).
starting_state_checks: You will not System.schedule in production
steps: Implement LAB_AllocQueueable and enqueue it from a LAB_Order__c after-insert trigger on the success path.
Implement LAB_ArchiveBatch with a QueryLocator and execute that updates a LAB_ checkbox in bulk.
Implement LAB_ArchiveSched whose execute only executeBatch's the archive class; schedule it once from anonymous Apex with a unique name.
Write a test with Test.startTest/stopTest that asserts the Queueable's LAB_ field change; abort the scheduled job in cleanup.
guided_completion: If enqueue happens before a thrown DmlException, the job should be absent—if it is present, you committed.
If Schedulable.execute performs per-record DML, move that to Batch.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: From the Queueable, chain one child with a delay of 1 minute; explain the 1-job async enqueue limit and the DE/Trial depth of 5.
evidence: AsyncApexJob query screenshot with LAB_ job names
Written mapping: Queueable vs Batch vs Scheduled vs Future
hands_on_lab.limitations: This lab does not prove daily 250,000 capacity or true parallel batch contention.

decision_table.signal: After a trigger save you need a callout and want to pass the LAB_Order__c sObject plus a job Id.
decision_table.choose: Queueable Apex with System.enqueueJob on the success path.
decision_table.not: @future that takes the sObject, or doing the callout in the trigger after DML.
decision_table.why: Asynchronous Apex + Queueable pages: complex types, job Id, recommended over future.

decision_table.signal: Nightly maintenance over millions of rows that would exceed a normal SOQL retrieved-row cap.
decision_table.choose: Batch Apex whose start returns a QueryLocator (Guide: up to 50 million).
decision_table.not: One Queueable that queries all rows, or 50 futures from a loop.
decision_table.why: Batch QueryLocator bypasses the usual retrieved-row governor; futures cannot take sObjects and fan-out hits daily async.

decision_table.signal: The job must run at 02:00 every night.
decision_table.choose: Scheduled Apex whose execute only kicks Batch or Queueable.
decision_table.not: Heavy DML inside Schedulable.execute, or System.schedule from a 200-row trigger.
decision_table.why: Scheduler: 100 concurrent (DE 5), runs as system, execution may delay; scheduled jobs use sync limits.

decision_table.signal: You must insert a User with a role in the same user gesture as Account DML.
decision_table.choose: Future method (or Queueable) to isolate mixed DML, as the Future Methods topic describes.
decision_table.not: Same-transaction mixed DML, or a new Batch solely for mixed DML.
decision_table.why: Future Methods: isolate DML on different sObject types to avoid mixed DML; still prefer Queueable when it fits.

decision_table.signal: You are already in Batch execute or a future method and need another background job.
decision_table.choose: Enqueue at most one Queueable (async enqueue limit 1); do not call @future from batch/future (0 allowed).
decision_table.not: 50 System.enqueueJob from the execute method, or @future from @future.
decision_table.why: Governors: enqueueJob async limit 1; future allowed 0 in batch and future contexts.

decision_table.signal: Parent trigger DML might fail after you enqueue.
decision_table.choose: Enqueue only after successful DML / on a path that will commit; accept that rollback drops the job.
decision_table.not: Rely on Apex Jobs to 'always' show the enqueue.
decision_table.why: Queueable and Future pages: jobs queued by a rolled-back transaction are not processed.

limitations: Does not teach HTTP mocking (APEX-013) or test.startTest depth (APEX-016) beyond the enqueue pattern.
Does not replace platform events (APEX-012) for fan-out to external subscribers.
Elastic async (beta) is cited only as a neighboring governor topic.
Limit numbers are Summer '26 / API 67.0 from the cited Guide pages.
security_notes: Scheduled Apex runs as system—permission on the class is not a user-mode substitute (APEX-015).
Do not put session IDs in Queueable member variables.
without sharing Batch classes still need an explicit CRUD/FLS story.
common_mistakes: New code using @future because 'that is how we used to do callouts.'
System.schedule inside a trigger on every row.
Assuming scheduled Apex gets async CPU (60,000 ms); it uses synchronous limits.
Enqueue from a transaction that later rolls back, then debugging Apex Jobs.
Starting multiple child Queueables from one executing job.

flashcards.front: New callout with a job Id?
flashcards.back: Queueable, not @future, unless mixed DML or a documented exception.

interview_questions.question: When do you use Queueable vs Batch vs Future vs Scheduled?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Queueable for job Id, sObjects, chaining, and most callouts. Batch for huge QueryLocator volumes. Scheduled for the clock. Future only for mixed DML or legacy. Salesforce recommends Queueable over future.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from the Asynchronous Apex table, not from habit. Volume that would blow a normal retrieved-row cap goes to Batch. A clock goes to Schedulable that only kicks Batch. After-save callout with an Account in memory is Queueable. I cite 50/1 enqueue, 5+100 batch, 100 scheduled, and daily 250k-or-licenses×200 from the governors page. I mention parent rollback drops queued jobs so I enqueue on the success path.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ order allocator as Queueable; nightly LAB_ case archive as Batch; weekly System.schedule of that batch.
tradeoffs: Flex Queue scarcity vs Queueable flexibility
follow_ups: Where do cursors plus Queueable fit?

interview_questions.question: Why does Salesforce recommend Queueable over future methods?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same use cases plus a job Id, non-primitive members, and chaining. Future is static void primitives only and cannot call future from future.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I can monitor AsyncApexJob for Queueable. I can hold a LAB_Order__c. I can chain one child (async enqueue limit 1). Future still matters for mixed DML examples in the Guide. I will not pass sObjects into @future. I will not fan out futures from a queueable without a daily-async plan.
interview_questions.example: Replace pingAllocator(Id) @future with LAB_AllocQueueable holding the order.
follow_ups: What is the DE chain depth?
How do you delay a Queueable?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling future 'deprecated' without the recommendation quote

interview_questions.question: You need to archive 2 million LAB_ cases nightly. Defend Batch over Queueable.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Batch QueryLocator can return up to 50 million and bypasses the usual SOQL retrieved-row governor. Each execute resets governors. Queueable is one transaction at a time unless you chain with a halt/delay.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also respect org caps: 5 active batch, 100 Holding. If Flex Queue is saturated, the async overview points at cursors plus Queueable as an alternative—I name that page rather than designing it here. Scheduled Apex kicks the batch at 02:00; execute stays thin because scheduled jobs use sync limits. Daily async counts start/execute/finish.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ArchiveBatch start returns getQueryLocator for closed cases; Schedulable only executeBatch's it.
tradeoffs: Chunk commits vs one Queueable heap
follow_ups: What if start uses an Iterable?
How do you test one execute?
weak_answer_warnings: Querying 2 million rows in a trigger

interview_questions.question: A trigger System.schedules a class for every Account insert. What goes wrong?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You can exceed 100 concurrent scheduled Apex jobs. Bulk API and UI mass edits make this worse. The Scheduler topic warns you must guarantee the trigger will not add more than the limit.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use a named singleton schedule, or Platform Events/Queueable for per-record follow-up. I query CronTrigger before scheduling. Developer Edition's 5 is even tighter. I do not hide this in a managed package without a unique job name strategy.
interview_questions.example: 200-row Data Loader insert creating 200 CronTrigger rows until the 100th throws.
weak_answer_warnings: Saying the platform deduplicates job names automatically without checking

interview_questions.question: Scheduled Apex execute does heavy SOQL/DML. Why is that a trap?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Governors: although scheduled Apex is async, synchronous per-transaction limits apply. You get 100 SOQL and 10,000 ms CPU, not the async 200 / 60,000 ms.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep Schedulable.execute as a dispatcher: Database.executeBatch or enqueueJob. That also keeps the class easier to deploy when jobs are active. I monitor CronTrigger, not only Apex Jobs. Actual execution can delay based on service availability—I do not promise 02:00:00.000.
follow_ups: How do you update a scheduled class?
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming scheduled jobs get async heap/CPU

interview_questions.question: Too many queueable jobs added to the queue. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check context: 50 in sync, 1 in async. Loops in triggers enqueue 200 times. From Batch execute you only get one child.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce with Limits.getQueueableJobs(). I collapse to one Queueable that accepts a list of Ids. I do not switch to 50 @future as a workaround—future has its own 50/0/50 matrix and shares daily async. I remember rollback drops jobs, so a retry storm can be a failed parent plus a loop.
interview_questions.example: Account trigger enqueueing LAB_AllocQueueable inside for(Account a : Trigger.new).
tradeoffs: One job with a list vs N jobs
Queueable vs Batch for the list
weak_answer_warnings: Raising a 'limit in Setup' that does not exist

interview_questions.question: How do daily async executions work, and who shares them?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: DailyAsyncApexExecutions is 250,000 or licenses × 200, whichever is greater. Batch start, execute, and finish each count. Future, Queueable, and scheduled share the same pool.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Batch preemptively checks capacity; the governors page example throws AsyncApexExecutions Limit exceeded if the job needs 10,000 and 9,500 remain. I would query the REST limits resource rather than guessing. Elastic async (beta) is extra throttled capacity—I will not design to it without reading that page. Delay-0 Queueable chains can burn the pool; the Queueable page says to implement a halt.
interview_questions.example: A 9,500-remaining org cannot start a 10,000-execute batch.
tradeoffs: Preemptive Batch fail vs silent throttle
follow_ups: Does Test.startTest consume daily async the same way?

interview_questions.question: When is @future still the right answer in 2026?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When you are isolating mixed DML as in the Future Methods example, or maintaining a documented legacy callout that cannot move yet. New job-Id/callout/sObject work should be Queueable.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still respect future rules: static void, primitives, callout=true, no future-from-future, 0 from batch context. I pass Ids and re-query. I mention the 2,000 unprocessed-request delay warning on the Future page as a fairness issue, not a hard governor. I do not pretend future is gone from the Guide.
interview_questions.example: Util.insertUserWithRole as @future while MixedDMLFuture inserts Account, per the Future Methods topic.
follow_ups: Can Queueable also isolate mixed DML?
weak_answer_warnings: Banning future in interviews as if the Guide deleted it
